To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$ and show that strong stratification can enhance the stability.
item.dc:creator: Yiting Yao

item.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $\Gamma=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $\Gamma$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.
item.dc:creator: S\'ergio L. N. Neves, Angela Pistoia

item.title: The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every orbitally stable soliton of the pure-power generalized Benjamin--Bona--Mahony (gBBM) equation is locally asymptotically stable. For both nonlinearities $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u$ and $f(u)=|u|^p$, the result holds for every exponent $p>1$ throughout the orbital stability range $c>c^*(p)$. Solutions starting sufficiently close to one of these solitons in the energy space converge locally in a moving frame to a nearby soliton and the limiting soliton has a speed close to that of the initial soliton. This establishes, for pure-power gBBM, the local convergence predicted by Bona and Soyeur's asymptotic stability conjecture and addresses an open problem raised by Martel. The proof uses Kato smoothing to close the high-energy virial estimates. The required smoothing estimates rely on the absence of nonzero embedded eigenvalues of the linearized operator. We establish this spectral property for every $p>1$ and every soliton speed $c>1$, including speeds for which the soliton is orbitally unstable. This settles a Pego--Weinstein spectral conjecture in the pure-power gBBM case.
item.dc:creator: Scipio Cuccagna, Daniele Del Santo, Masaya Maeda

item.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system with localized boundary data in the half-space
item.description: arXiv:2611.00998v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and nonnegative, space-time separable boundary data supported in the unit ball and in $[0,1]$, respectively. A separation point is a pair $(x',t)$, with $x'$ outside the spatial support, arbitrarily near which a velocity component takes both signs. The main ingredient is an explicit representation of the velocity and pressure via confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, if the temporal boundary data are regular and unimodal, log-concavity yields a unique separation time for the $i$th tangential component at every boundary point with $|x_i|>1$, and exactly two for the normal component at distant points, one before and one after the boundary data vanish. The later one, a simple zero of the second normal derivative of the normal component at the boundary, is unique even without unimodality. We obtain monotonicity and asymptotics of separation times and vanishing rates of normal derivatives. For tangential boundary data with $n\geq3$, under the same assumptions, a separation time for the velocity component in their direction exists at $x'$ with $|x'|>1$ precisely when the corresponding Riesz transform of the spatial boundary data has a positive derivative in that direction at $x'$, and log-concavity makes it unique. For the remaining components, we prove existence and uniqueness of separation points on distant lines parallel to the axes, with asymptotics in terms of spatial moments and support geometry. For radial spatial boundary data, we determine the signs and zero sets of tangential pressure derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Kyungkeun Kang, Chanhong Min

item.title: Local energy decay for small radial solutions of the two-dimensional Hamiltonian $abcd$ Boussinesq system
item.description: arXiv:2611.23995v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the $abcd$ Boussinesq system in two space dimensions, a four-parameter family of models for the two-way propagation of small-amplitude long surface waves, in the generic regime $a,c<0$, $b,d>0$. We first revisit the local well-posedness theory in Sobolev spaces in dimensions $2\le n\le4$ and show that for the Hamiltonian case $b=d$ the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed for small data in the energy space $\mathbb{H}^1(\mathbb R^n)$. Then we consider the asymptotic behavior of these global solutions in the $n=2$ case. Under the condition $-a,-c>b/9$, we prove that every small solution with radial symmetry exhibits local energy decay. As a consequence, there are no small radial time-periodic (in particular, stationary) solutions. Decay also holds, along sequences of times, on balls whose radius grows almost linearly in time. The proof is based on new virial identities adapted to the radial structure of the system. In the proof we introduce two correction functionals such that the resulting quadratic form is coercive precisely when $-a,-c>b/9$, a threshold which is sharp for the functional. To our knowledge this is the first result describing the long-time dynamics of $abcd$ systems in dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Chulkwang Kwak, Claudio Mu\~noz

item.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.27493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(\Omega, \mathcal F_0; L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.
item.dc:creator: Bikram Podder, Surendra Kumar

item.title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.30663v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).
item.dc:creator: Egor Baitenov, Stefano Modena

item.title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.30664v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of arXiv:2611.30663 from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.
item.dc:creator: Egor Baitenov, Stefano Modena

item.title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
item.description: arXiv:2611.32419v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es La\'in-Sanclemente

item.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2611.10598v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long

item.title: Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
item.description: arXiv:2611.28903v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) parts.Their weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.
item.dc:creator: Mark Spivack

item.title: The polygonal Weinstock inequality and quantitative stability
item.description: arXiv:2611.32028v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes the perimeter-normalized first positive Steklov eigenvalue $J(P) = |\partial P|\sigma_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity. More generally, if $P$ has $p$ strictly convex vertices and $q$ reflex vertices after merging consecutive collinear sides, then $J(P) \le J(R_{p+\min(q,2)})$, with equality if and only if $q = 0$ and $P$ is similar to $R_p$. Among polygons with at most $N$ sides, restricting to those that are nonconvex or have fewer than $N$ genuine sides lowers the supremum of $J$ by $12\pi\zeta(3)N^{-4} + O(N^{-5})$ as $N \to \infty$, with a positive gap for every $N \ge 4$. For convex $p$-gons, the spectral deficit $J(R_p) - J(P)$ controls the normalized squared deviations of support heights, midpoint offsets, and side lengths with weights $1$, $p^{-2}$, and $p^{-3}$, as well as $p^{-3}$ times the sum of squared exterior-angle deviations from $2\pi/p$; the length weight $p^{-3}$ is sharp. For triangles, the deficit is instead comparable to the square root of the relative area deficit at fixed perimeter, or equivalently to $1 - r$, where $r$ is the singular-value ratio of an affine map from an equilateral triangle. Independently of the number of reflex vertices, a boundary phase identity in arc-length balanced disk coordinates yields the sharp fourth-order bound $2\pi/J(P) - 1 \ge 2\zeta(3)p^{-3} + 8\zeta(4)p^{-4} + O(p^{-5})$. For fixed $p$, a degree-$p$ Blaschke transport links this identity to $H^{1/p}$ coercivity for the regularized square root of the conformal derivative, perimeter-concentration rigidity at equally spaced convex prevertices, and quadratic Hausdorff stability for $p \ge 4$.
item.dc:creator: Zhuo Cheng, Yian Zhang
